question: According to the fluid mosaic model (流動鑲嵌模型), what are the two main chemical components of a cell membrane?
options: Cellulose and proteins / 纖維素和蛋白質
Phospholipids and proteins / 磷脂和蛋白質
Starch and phospholipids / 澱粉和磷脂
Glycogen and cholesterol / 糖原和膽固醇

question: How are phospholipid molecules arranged in the cell membrane?
options: A single layer with hydrophilic heads facing the cytoplasm
A bilayer with hydrophobic tails pointing inwards towards each other
A bilayer with hydrophilic heads pointing inwards towards each other
A random network embedded in cellulose fibres

question: The hydrophobic core of the phospholipid bilayer prevents polar and charged ions from passing freely through the membrane.
Which component of the cell membrane helps maintain membrane fluidity (流動性) and stability at varying temperatures?
What is the primary role of glycoproteins (糖蛋白) on the outer surface of the cell membrane?
options: Cell recognition and cell-to-cell communication / 細胞識別

question: Diffusion (擴散) is an active process that requires energy from ATP to move molecules down a concentration gradient.
Which of the following substances crosses the phospholipid bilayer directly by simple diffusion?
Which factor would DECREASE the rate of diffusion across a cell membrane?
options: Increasing the surface area of the membrane
Increasing the thickness (diffusion distance) of the membrane
Increasing the steepness of the concentration gradient

question: Facilitated diffusion (促進擴散) uses carrier proteins or channel proteins to transport substances down a concentration gradient without using ATP.
Osmosis (滲透) is defined as the net movement of water molecules across a differentially permeable membrane from a region of _________ to a region of _________.
options: lower water potential; higher water potential
higher water potential; lower water potential
higher solute concentration; lower solute concentration
lower water concentration; higher water concentration

question: What is the water potential (水勢) of pure distilled water at atmospheric pressure?
Dissolving more solute in water increases its water potential.
What happens to human red blood cells when placed in a hypotonic solution (低滲溶液) such as distilled water?
options: They swell and eventually burst (haemolysis / 溶血).

question: Why does a plant cell NOT burst when placed in pure water?
options: Water stops entering the cell immediately.
The strong, rigid cellulose cell wall resists further expansion.
The cell membrane becomes impermeable to water.
Active transport pumps water out at the same rate.

question: Plasmolysis (質壁分離) occurs when a plant cell is placed in a hypertonic solution (高滲溶液) and the cell membrane pulls away from the cell wall.
Which process moves mineral ions into root hair cells against a concentration gradient?
Which metabolic inhibitor would directly stop active transport (主動轉運) in root hair cells?
options: A chemical that inhibits aerobic respiration and ATP production
A chemical that increases membrane fluidity
A dye that stains cellulose cell walls
An enzyme that breaks down extracellular starch

question: Carrier proteins (載體蛋白) involved in active transport change shape using energy from ATP to move specific molecules across the membrane.
How do white blood cells engulf bacteria into the cell?
options: By facilitated diffusion through channel proteins
By phagocytosis (吞噬作用), a form of endocytosis

question: In an investigation using potato strips immersed in sucrose solutions of different concentrations, one strip shows no change in mass. What does this indicate?
options: The sucrose solution is pure distilled water.
The water potential of the sucrose solution equals the water potential of the potato cells.
The potato cells have died and lost differential permeability.
No water molecules are moving in or out of the cells.

question: When a plant cell is flaccid (軟縮), it loses turgidity, causing herbaceous plants to wilt (凋謝).
Which of the following processes requires membrane fusion and ATP to transport large proteins out of a secretory cell?
Boiling beetroot tissue damages the cell membrane proteins and phospholipid bilayer, causing red pigment to leak out into surrounding water.

[OSMOSIS & WATER POTENTIAL] Strips of raw potato tissue of equal initial mass were placed in two different sucrose solutions: Solution X (0.1 M) and Solution Y (0.8 M). After 1 hour, the potato strip in Solution X increased in mass and felt firm, whereas the strip in Solution Y decreased in mass and felt soft. 1) Explain the change in mass and texture of the potato strip in Solution Y in terms of water potential. 2) State the condition of the potato cells in Solution X.
rubric: To score full points, the response must demonstrate structural mastery: 1) Solution Y (0.8 M sucrose) has a lower water potential than the potato cell sap, so water moves out of the potato cells into Solution Y by osmosis across the differentially permeable cell membrane; as cells lose water, they lose turgidity and become flaccid (or plasmolysed), making the strip soft and lighter. 2) The potato cells in Solution X are turgid.

question: [ACTIVE TRANSPORT & RESPIRATION] A student investigates the uptake of nitrate ions (NO3-) by young barley roots under two conditions: Set-up A is bubbled with air (oxygen), while Set-up B is bubbled with nitrogen gas (no oxygen). The rate of nitrate uptake is much higher in Set-up A than in Set-up B. 1) Identify the main mechanism responsible for nitrate uptake in Set-up A. 2) Explain why bubbling with nitrogen gas in Set-up B greatly reduces nitrate uptake.
rubric: To score full points, the response must demonstrate structural mastery: 1) Active transport. 2) Nitrogen gas creates anaerobic conditions (lack of oxygen), which prevents aerobic respiration in root hair cells; as a result, insufficient ATP is generated to power the carrier proteins required for active transport of nitrate ions against a concentration gradient.
